name: Hora, Winter
body:
WINTER HORA
CR 6

This beautiful woman appears enveloped in a cold, crystalline aura; her skin and hair are pale, her eyes and clothes as blue as deep ice.

XP 2,400
CG Medium fey
Init +8; Senses low-light vision; Perception +16
Aura paralyzing beauty (30 ft., DC 19)

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 15, flat-footed 14 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +4 natural)
hp 65 (10d6+30)
Fort +6, Ref +11, Will +10
DR 5/cold iron; Resist cold 10
Weaknesses winter bound

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee rime blade +9 (3d6+3 piercing +1d6 cold)
Ranged ray of frost +9 (4d8 cold)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 10th; concentration +14)

Constant—speak with animals, speak with plants
At will—know direction, light, pass without trace
1/day—alarm, bestow curse (DC 18), commune with nature, faerie fire, snowball (DC 15)

STATISTICS

Str 12, Dex 19, Con 16, Int 15, Wis 17, Cha 18
Base Atk +5; CMB +6, CMD 21
Feats Combat Casting, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Mobility, Weapon Finesse
Skills Acrobatics +17, Diplomacy +17, Escape Artist +17, Knowledge (nature) +15, Perception +16, Sense Motive +16, Stealth +17, Survival +13
Languages Common, Elven, Sylvan; speak with animals, speak with plants
SQ winter’s wellness

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Paralyzing Beauty (Su)

This ability affects all humanoids within 30 feet of the winter hora. Those who look directly at the hora must succeed on a DC 19 Fortitude save or be exhausted for 1 minute and fatigued for 1 hour. The hora can suppress or resume this ability as a free action. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Winter Bound (Su)

During summer months, the winter hora gains the sickened condition.

Winter’s Wellness (Su)

As an immediate action after a winter hora or an ally within 30 feet of the hora that it can see fails a saving throw, the hora grants an enhancement bonus to the saving throw based on the time of year. The bonus is +4 during the month of the winter solstice, +2 during the month before or after the winter solstice, and +1 during any time other than the summer solstice month, during which this ability doesn’t function. The winter hora can’t use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate forests
Organization solitary or chorus (2-12)
Treasure standard (rime blade, other treasure)

The Horai in the Greek myth were nymphs who danced around the Sun’s chariot, representing the seasons of the year and the hours of the day (the word “hour” derives from the Ancient Greek and Latin Hora). There were most commonly three of them: Thallo, Auxo, and Carpo (“Bloom” for Spring, “Increaser” for Summer, and “Reaper of Fruits” for Autumn). In other versions, they were the embodiment of the good effects of law and order (symbolized by Apollo) on the world of mortals, and their names were Eunomia (“Good Governance”), Dike (“Justice”), and Eirene (“Peace”). In Pathfinder’s rules, the stats for the Summer Hora and the Summer Hora Queen were given in the Faerie Bestiary: here we present horai for the remaining three seasons, and their respective Queens. Maybe the nymphs of Order could be discussed in a future issue of this magazine?
